text:
B: Hi, hi. Can you hear me? Sorry, it's... yeah. Hi.
A: Yeah. Alright, mate.
B: Matthew, Norwich.
A: Dean. You're the river bloke.
B: Ha, I'm the river bloke, apparently. Has everyone said?
A: Leanne said you'd be handy at her pub quiz.
B: Oh God, only if it's the geography round. Anything else, I'm useless. Do you do one?
A: Thursdays. Mostly for the pint. I'm alright on sport.
B: Same, Thursdays, work lot. We came fourth last week out of five. The one team below us was two people.
A: Ha. That's still a win.
B: That's what I said! Erm, what do you drink? Sorry, random question.
A: Stella. Carling if it's on. You?
B: I'm a bit of a, er, Norwich has loads of real ale pubs, so I've sort of been converted. I won't bore you.
A: Yeah, don't. Warm beer with a name like Old Badger's Whatever.
B: Ha, that's about right, to be fair. You into football then?
A: Gillingham. Lost Saturday. Chelsea on the telly.
B: Norwich City. Well, lapsed. I still check every score though, which isn't very lapsed, is it.
A: Nah, that's not lapsed, mate, that's just ashamed.
B: Ha, yeah, that's fair. That's very fair. I go a few times a season with an old uni mate. Do you play at all?
A: Used to. Five-a-side Wednesdays. Packed it in.
B: Oh, why?
A: Had a row with a lad on the other team. Bit of a scene. Didn't go back.
B: Oh, right. Yeah, there's always one, isn't there. We've got a bloke who thinks it's the Champions League final every week. Slide tackles on astroturf, you know, takes the skin off your leg. I play Wednesdays too, when I remember to answer the group chat, which is maybe half the time. I'm a bit rubbish at replying to things generally, to be honest. Sorry, I'm rambling.
A: You're alright. Yeah, ours was like that. To be fair I gave as good as I got.
B: Do you miss it?
A: Bit, yeah. Can't be bothered with the hassle though. I walk everywhere instead, 'cause I won't pay for parking.
B: Ha, that's a good reason. I cycle in summer, then it rains and I'm on the bus, and the bus is always late.
A: Rains a lot in Norwich then?
B: Most of autumn. Which is, erm, good for business, I suppose. Bad for my bus.
A: Ha. Silver lining. What, so floods, you get paid more?
B: Not really more, just busier. And you see people's houses, after. That's the bit that's, er, not great.
A: Yeah. Must be grim, that.
B: It can be. Anyway. Sorry. What do you do, I've heard plumbing?
A: Supplies. Invoices, phones. Coffee machine's broke three weeks. You'll have heard that and all.
